text:
You will suffer. You have suffered already.
Perhaps you are suffering now.
And though you know
why (if indeed you know),
that knowledge will not console you.

The farewell to your own; chance,
relentless; the mystery of the sky,
everything lost, facts and life below, time below,
or life above too, toward what awaits you,
everything shapes the taste of your tears,
a tasteless taste, since it is not shared
by the one who has seen you suffer
—cannot share it—,
a taste you do not understand,
a heap of tears that trace,
I do not know where, a sea
on which they sail, and I do not know why,
useless forever, inconsolable,
who knows since when,
their soul,
your soul
and mine.

translation.title: The Sleeping Animal
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The poem’s repeated, inward address and its final convergence of three souls are preserved.
